dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}! Is this where you usually reside?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Looks like you've got plenty of space! It feels a little empty though. Ever thought about inviting a few more people over to hang out, or maybe throwing a party?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I like it a lot. Couldn't think of a better place to say my prayers!

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I haven't found a drinking spot just yet, though. Don't suppose I could persuade you to build a bar here?

choices.text: Is it... okay for a deacon to drink so much?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Barbatos brought us seeds and rain on a gentle breeze, so to show our gratitude, we brewed wine from his generous gifts.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Good wine is not only a blessing from the Anemo Archon — it's a symbol of Mondstadt itself.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Given all this, as a member of the Church of Favonius, it'd be far more improper of me to abstain entirely. Wouldn't you agree?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Wonderful! I know plenty of tavern owners, so leave the drinks procurement to me...

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Oh, and how about a bard to liven things up a little? I know just the right person.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Sure thing! In fact, I've got just the story to share.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm all ears.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As the deacon, I occasionally offer life advice. Recently, a couple approached me separately, each seeking my counsel.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The husband, a handsome knight and excellent swordsman, was the owner of a treasured family heirloom — an incredibly sharp sword.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, he lacked a suitably valuable sheath, so he usually kept it wrapped in a roll of cloth.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: His wife was a beautiful gardener with a passion for cultivation. Recently, her many years of hard work had finally paid off with the blooming of a rare and stunning flower.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, having no greenhouse of her own, she had to keep the delicate flower at an associate's place.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As the holidays approached, both husband and wife hoped to surprise each other with the perfect thoughtful gift.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: As you may have guessed, the husband wished to present his wife with a greenhouse of her own. However, being of modest means, his only way to secure the necessary funds was by selling off his sword.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: The wife, on the other hand, wished to give her husband an exquisitely crafted sheath to go with his sword. Like her husband, she could only achieve this by selling away her most prized possession.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Both of them came to ask me if they should make the sacrifice. Which would you have advised to go through with it?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Mm. The quality of a knight's own swordsmanship is indeed far more important than that of their sword. So he should accept the loss and help his wife fulfill her dream.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Still, if his wife ever learned that he had traded in his treasure for her dream, would she really be pleased to accept the gift?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: After all, you can always grow new flowers, even rare ones. But his sword was truly one of a kind.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: In either case, you could argue that trading in their treasure would be a huge mistake. There was no way to do them both justice.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So did you end up turning them both away?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: And ask them to hide their affection? Now, why would I do that? That would only have led to regret. No, this was a rare opportunity to encourage a pair of lovers to break the day-to-day monotony, embrace the festive spirit, and do something truly romantic!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... What did you do?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Isn't it obvious? I encouraged both of them to make the trade-off!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: I suppose you think I gave them even more cause for regret, huh?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Quite the opposite... If their real goal was to show the other how much they cared, then neither the sword nor the flower truly mattered.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Just imagine the scene when they finally exchanged gifts with each other. I'm sure that made for a festival that neither one of them will ever forget.

choices.text: Wow, what a stroke of genius!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: #You get me, {NICKNAME}! Neither object was all that important in comparison to a person's love for their partner.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Ah, yes. Even though she would no longer be able to tend to her beloved flower, she could be sure that it would continue to flourish.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: It could still thrive under the care of a fellow master, while her husband's long-time wish would finally be fulfilled.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Still, if her husband ever learned that she had traded in her finest work to grant his wish, would he really be pleased to accept the gift?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: His wife had devoted years of her life to the cultivation of that flower, while the sword was simply something he'd inherited from his father. In other words, he'd done nothing to earn it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Hmm... Wanna join me in some choir practice?

choices.text: Sounds like something I'd be good at!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Just so you know, in choir singing, there's no "I," only "we." The goal is perfect harmony, like how the sounds of the world all blend seamlessly into the wind.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Still, self-confidence is important. Newcomers to the choir are often too shy or afraid to sing.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Why don't we do some vocal warm-ups? Here, like so...

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: I did give it some serious thought, but ended up deciding against it.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh? Why?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Idols have to be able to greet their fans with energy and enthusiasm. Being kind by nature, Barbara is always happy to oblige...

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: But I struggle to spend time with people I find boring, which just so happens to be most of them...

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: And when it comes to those who bore me, all I can muster up is the bare-bones minimum.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: So, I prefer to stay on the sidelines, observing how Barbara lives up to people's expectations of an idol.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: I won't lie — I find that far more satisfying than being an idol myself.

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Wait, do YOU want to be an idol? We still don't have an idol from the Knights just yet! The Honorary Knight of Mondstadt, now the first Knight-Idol of the land... Just thinking about it is making me giddy!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Just leave the voice lessons to me. You'll be ready to make your debut in no time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh, think I'll pass...

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Aww, what's the harm in trying? Come on, just follow my lead...

choices.text: Ever thought about making your own debut as an idol?
What if I can't carry a tune?

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: Haha, no problem at all!

response.speaker: Dahlia
response.text: None of our hymns are technically difficult. I'm sure you'll be able to find your voice as long as you put some genuine emotion into it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Dahlia.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: #Morning, {NICKNAME}! I was just about to go lead the morning prayers. Wanna come watch? I'm gonna ask Lord Barbatos a pretty interesting question today...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Dahlia.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Good night. I just finished my evening prayers — may your dreams tonight be filled with peace and joy.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I really love the layout of this courtyard! It reminds me of the times I've gone mischief-hunting all over Mondstadt. I can't help but feel like there's still something missing, though...

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: Oh, I know! We need... a bard performing in front of a crowd, a little girl secretly tossing bombs into the fountain, and a knight lounging lazily on the bench.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: If we can get them all together in one place, the atmosphere would be just perfect.

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: I have this exact set of furniture in the room I was given by the Church. Seeing it here feels like coming home!

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: #Thank you, O great {NICKNAME}, for all you've done to adorn this world. Allow me to compose an ode to exalt your efforts!

dialogues.speaker: Dahlia
dialogues.text: ...What? Too dramatic?
